clue.text: Uncle Pepe included in the county's prayers

indicators.note: the uncle's word is placed within the county's name, as something included in it

parts.note: Devon is an English county in the south-west; its possessive gives the letters with S
Pepe is a Spanish name, so his uncle is a tio, the Spanish word for uncle

explanation.surface: A Spanish relative joins in the prayers said across an English county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'included in' puts TIO, Spanish for uncle (Pepe being a Spanish name), inside DEVONS. DEVON is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Devotions are acts of worship, particularly private prayers.

clue.text: A note in dire lament

indicators.note: the musical letter is set inside the word dire, which encloses it

parts.note: G is one of the notes of the musical scale

explanation.surface: A single note sounded within a gloomy, mournful lament.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirge is a mournful song sung for the dead, a funeral lament.

clue.text: Went to see flying bomb in position

parts.note: the V1 was the German flying bomb of the Second World War, written here as VI
something sited has been placed in position

explanation.surface: Someone inspected the spot where a flying bomb had landed.
explanation.walkthrough: The V1 (doodlebug) was the German flying bomb that fell on London; its 1 is written as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Visited means called on, paid a call to someone or somewhere.

clue.text: Like the Greek quad

parts.note: a quad is a quadrangle, a four-cornered courtyard; the Greek for four-angled describes the same shape

explanation.surface: Resembling the courtyard of a Greek college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quad' suggests a college courtyard, but it is short for quadrangle; put into Greek, four (tetra) plus angled (-gonal) gives the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Tetragonal means having four angles, exactly what a quadrangle has, expressed in Greek roots.

clue.text: Cats in a pound ?

explanation.definitionFit: The ounce is the snow leopard, a big cat; and a pound weight holds sixteen of the units of that name.

clue.text: Sprang, and the Spanish shortly put to flight

parts.note: Sp is the standard short form of Spanish
an army routed is put to flight

explanation.surface: Spanish forces jumped up and the enemy was quickly chased off.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprouted means sprang up, as shoots appear from the ground.

clue.text: Funny, there's nothing in numerals

indicators.note: the zero is placed inside the run of Roman figures, which surround it

parts.note: C, M, I and C are all Roman numerals
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A joke about there being no zero among the figures.
explanation.walkthrough: Roman numerals have no zero, which is the joke of the surface; here CMIC, a run of them, has O placed among them.
explanation.definitionFit: Comic means amusing, causing laughter.

clue.text: Many a song about this earth

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a crossword stand-in for many
a lay is an old word for a song or ballad

explanation.surface: Countless ballads have been written about this land of ours.
explanation.definitionFit: Clay is a kind of soil, so it can stand for earth.

clue.text: Platform for a revolutionary at sea?

parts.note: the main is a poetic name for the open sea
a spinning top revolves, so it is something revolutionary

explanation.surface: A soapbox for a political rebel on board ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' suggests a rebel, but it is a spinning top; the maintop is the platform at the head of a ship's mainmast.
explanation.definitionFit: The maintop is the platform above the head of a ship's lower mainmast.

clue.text: Study the striking position of Woman

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
a stance is how a batsman or golfer stands to strike the ball

explanation.surface: Investigate the commanding posture of a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Woman' asks for a woman's name, here Constance.
explanation.definitionFit: Constance is a woman's given name.

clue.text: Prepare table again to cope with printer's pie

explanation.definitionFit: To lay the table once more is to set it anew; and pie is jumbled printing type, which a compositor must set afresh.

clue.text: Roundhead artist in race for a story

indicators.note: the head letter and the painter are placed inside the people, enclosed by them

parts.note: a race of people is a nation
read as the head of the word round, its first letter
RA is a Royal Academician, a recognised artist

explanation.surface: A Civil War Puritan painter takes part in a contest to tell a tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roundhead' suggests a Puritan soldier of the English Civil War, but here it is the head of 'round', R; with RA it goes 'in' NATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Narration is the telling of a tale, so it can mean a story.

clue.text: Additional one perhaps coming to us from outside

parts.note: something additional is extra

indicators.note: the letters of one may be arranged in another way, perhaps, so they are reordered

explanation.surface: An extra person, possibly, arrives to join us from elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' turns ONE into NEO; EXTRA comes first and US is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Extraneous means originating outside, foreign to the thing in question.

clue.text: Standing order for compositors

parts.note: the Latin instruction let it stand, marked on a proof to tell typesetters to keep a deleted correction

explanation.surface: A regular bank instruction given to typesetters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standing order' looks like a bank payment, but it is an order to let text stand, the proofreader's mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Stet, Latin for let it stand, tells the printer to ignore a marked correction.

clue.text: Wild peer can't for instance return a commission

indicators.note: wild letters are out of control, so the letters of these words are rearranged
to return is to go back, so these two letters are read backwards

explanation.surface: A furious nobleman cannot, say, give back his fee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' rearranges PEER and CANT to PERCENTA; 'return' turns EG into GE.
explanation.definitionFit: An agent's commission is often paid as a fraction of each hundred pounds of sales.

clue.text: Sets right-farewell amigo

parts.note: adios is the Spanish word of farewell, one a Spanish friend would say

explanation.surface: Fixes everything up and says goodbye to a Spanish pal.
explanation.definitionFit: Radio sets are receivers, so sets can mean wireless receivers.

clue.text: Listen again, to 'the girl at practice

parts.note: to rehear is to hear again, listen once more
Sal is a familiar girl's name, short for Sally

explanation.surface: Hearing a young woman once more while she practises.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsal is a practice run of a play or concert.

clue.text: Permanent juvenile role.

parts.note: the stage part of the boy who never grows up, in J M Barrie's play

explanation.surface: An acting part as a youngster for ever.
explanation.walkthrough: The boy who would not grow up in J M Barrie's play stays young permanently, and the role was traditionally a pantomime part.
explanation.definitionFit: Barrie's hero refuses to grow up, a juvenile for ever.

clue.text: River trap for catching fish

parts.note: the Seine is the river through Paris
the Seine is the river through Paris

explanation.surface: A snare set on a river to catch fish.
explanation.walkthrough: SEINE, the river through Paris, is followed by NET, which the definition's own word 'trap' also suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A seine net is a large fishing net hung vertically with floats and weights.

clue.text: Entertainer is getting on in years; gives pledges

parts.note: a host entertains guests
one who ages is growing older, getting on in years

explanation.surface: An ageing party-giver makes promises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pledges' here means people held as security, not promises.
explanation.definitionFit: Hostages are people handed over or held as security, an old sense of pledges.

clue.text: Something handy for a saboteur in the works

definitions.text: Something handy for a saboteur in the works

parts.words: Something handy for a saboteur in the works
parts.note: the tool proverbially thrown into the works to wreck them, in the phrase about spoiling plans

explanation.surface: A useful item for someone sabotaging a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: To throw a spanner in the works means to sabotage a plan; the tool is also handy in a workshop.
explanation.definitionFit: Throwing this wrench into machinery is the idiom for wrecking a scheme.

clue.text: Hard water ? That depends

parts.note: frozen water is literally hard, and one that hangs down de-pends

explanation.surface: Is the water hard? It all depends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard water' means limescale-heavy water, but here it is frozen water; 'depends' is read as hangs down.
explanation.definitionFit: An icicle is frozen water hanging down from an edge.

clue.text: Many praise one, a lady of Rome

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, standing for many
to laud is to praise
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Lots of people admire a certain Roman woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Claudia is a feminine Roman name, from the Claudian family.

clue.text: In prison again ? Just the place to do this

definitions.text: In prison again ? Just the place to do this

parts.words: In prison again ? Just the place to do this
parts.note: being penned up once more, ..., is the time to feel sorry for one's crimes

explanation.surface: Back in jail? The perfect spot for reflection.
explanation.walkthrough: Pen means prison, so 're-pent' would be penned up again, and prison is where one should feel remorse.
explanation.definitionFit: To feel remorse for wrongdoing is what a reoffending prisoner should do.

clue.text: Woe is me, giving back part of my salary

indicators.note: giving back means the letters are taken in the reverse order
the run of letters is a part of the words my salary

explanation.surface: Lamenting the return of some of one's wages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part of' picks SALA from 'my salary', and 'giving back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Alas is an exclamation of sorrow, like woe is me.

clue.text: Where some 'of that Welsh coal is ?

definitions.text: Where some 'of that Welsh coal is

parts.words: Where some 'of that Welsh coal is
parts.note: Neath is a town in the South Wales coalfield, so the coal lies below it

explanation.surface: Where can you find some of that Welsh coal?
explanation.walkthrough: Neath is a town in the South Wales coalfield; the coal is under Neath, read as one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Beneath, lower down, is where buried coal lies.

clue.text: Governor Ronald. gives us the bird…

parts.note: a colonial governor is addressed as HE, His Excellency
Ron is the short form of Ronald

explanation.surface: A governor called Ronald is booed by the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gives us the bird' suggests being jeered, a sense the next clue picks up; here the bird is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A heron is a long-legged wading bird.

clue.text: … and how a snake might give it?

definitions.text: and how a snake might give it?

parts.words: and how a snake might give it?
parts.note: it refers back to the bird of the previous clue: giving the bird means jeering, and a snake does that sound

explanation.surface: How might a snake show disapproval of the governor?
explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs on from 24: to give someone the bird is to jeer them, and snakes make that sibilant noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Hissing is how an audience gives the bird, and a snake's natural sound.

clue.text: In judgment one shows feeling

indicators.note: the numeral is placed in the court's decision, enclosed by it

parts.note: a sentence is a judge's judgment
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: In court, one defendant shows emotion at the ruling.
explanation.definitionFit: Sentience is the capacity to feel or perceive.

clue.text: A tree in the dale, perhaps? Right!

indicators.note: the letters of dale may perhaps be arranged otherwise, so they are reordered

explanation.surface: Asking whether a tree grows in the valley, and being told yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right!' reads as agreement but supplies R after the reordered DALE.
explanation.definitionFit: The alder is a tree of the birch family growing by water.

clue.text: Airborne frolics

explanation.definitionFit: Skylarks are songbirds famed for flight; and larks are pranks or high jinks.

clue.text: It comprehended the benefits of the Church's decimal system

definitions.text: It comprehended the benefits of the Church's decimal system

parts.words: It comprehended the benefits of the Church's decimal system
parts.note: comprehended means held, and the Church took a tenth of produce, stored in a farm building

explanation.surface: This understood the advantages of the Church's base-ten method.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comprehended' means contained, not understood; the decimal system is the Church's levy of a tenth of produce, stored in this barn.
explanation.definitionFit: A tithe barn stored the tenth of farm produce paid to the parish church.
